findings.stat_label: cashier's check fee, yours vs peer median
findings.headline: Your cashier's check fee is above the market range.
findings.body: At $10, it is $4 above the $6 peer median and the highest of the 8 peers that publish it (middle half of the market: $5–$8.25). It is infrequent and mostly a perception item.

findings.headline: Several lines are priced below the market.
findings.body: Your deposited-item return fee ($7.50 vs a $10 median) and outgoing international wire fee ($35 vs a $50 median) each sit below the peer 25th percentile. These are customer-favorable positions that peers' published schedules can verify. If the pricing is deliberate, it is worth stating plainly in account marketing.

findings.stat_label: comparable lines inside the market range
findings.headline: Most of your schedule is priced with the market.
findings.body: Of the 8 fee lines where we found both your published amount and at least eight comparable peers, five sit between the peer 25th and 75th percentiles, one above and two below.

exec_narrative: Forbright Bank is compared with 68 banks of similar size nationwide that publish fee schedules in the Bank Fee Index; a national set is used because fewer than 15 same-size peers in Maryland have published data, so local competitors may price differently. Of 8 rankable lines, five sit inside the middle half of the market, one above it (cashier's check fee), and two below it (deposited-item return fee and outgoing international wire fee). We would suggest three steps, in order of value: (1) review the cashier's check fee, which sits above the market range; the peer median of $6 is the reference point; (2) state the below-market deposited-item return fee in account marketing, where peers' published schedules make it verifiable; (3) check that the overdraft fee is published where customers can find it.

callouts.title: Cashier's check fee — $10
callouts.stat: Peer median $6 · middle half $5–$8.25 · range $5–$10 · 100th percentile · n=8
callouts.body: Published as “Cashier's Check.” At $10 it is $4 above the $6 peer median. It is infrequent and mostly a perception item. Holding the premium is reasonable if the service behind it is differentiated; otherwise the peer median of $6 is the reference point.

callouts.title: Deposited-item return fee — $7.50
callouts.stat: Peer median $10 · middle half $9.63–$11.50 · 23rd percentile · n=22
callouts.body: Published as “Return Deposit Item.” This is a customer-favorable position. If it is a deliberate choice, it belongs in account marketing; if it is an old price that was never revisited, the median of $10 is the reference point.

callouts.title: Outgoing international wire fee — $35
callouts.stat: Peer median $50 · middle half $40–$50 · 11th percentile · n=9
callouts.body: Published as “Outgoing International Wire Transfer.” A customer-favorable price on a low-volume line. No action is indicated unless it is an old price that was never revisited, in which case the peer median of $50 is the reference point.

callouts.title: Fees we could not find in your published schedule
callouts.body: Absence here means the line was not in the documents listed in § 06, not that you do not charge it. Regulators and comparison sites increasingly expect the full consumer fee schedule to be posted in one place.

context_narrative:
Overdraft and returned-item fees have been the focus of regulatory and public attention since 2022, and many of the largest banks have reduced overdraft fees or eliminated NSF fees outright. Community institutions have moved more slowly and more unevenly, which is why the spread inside a peer set is often wider than the headline national averages suggest.

Fee schedules are also now public in a practical sense: they are collected, compared and summarized automatically. A customer or examiner comparing Forbright Bank with its peers sees the same published lines this report uses, so the schedule is a positioning document as much as a pricing one.

How to use this report: § 02 shows every line against the peer range; § 03 explains the lines that sit outside it; § 05 names peers line by line. Ranked comparisons require at least eight peers publishing the same line. Where your institution offers several amounts for one category, the report uses the standard consumer charge described in the methodology below.
